questions.question: Spinal epidural lipomatosis is a non-neoplastic overgrowth of fat that characteristically follows the signal of which tissue on all MRI sequences?
questions.detail: Spinal epidural lipomatosis is a non-neoplastic overgrowth of fat that characteristically follows the signal of subcutaneous fat on all MRI sequences.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of spinal epidural lipomatosis?
questions.detail: The most common cause of spinal epidural lipomatosis is steroid administration.

questions.question: In the mid-thoracic spine, an epidural fat thickness of greater than how many millimeters suggests the diagnosis of epidural lipomatosis?
questions.detail: In the mid-thoracic spine, an epidural fat thickness of greater than 6 mm suggests the diagnosis of epidural lipomatosis.

questions.question: In the lumbar spine, severe epidural lipomatosis characteristically creates which contour of the thecal sac?
questions.detail: In the lumbar spine, severe epidural lipomatosis characteristically creates a trefoil or Y-shaped contour of the thecal sac.

questions.question: Ossification of the spinal ligaments, such as OPLL, primarily affects which patient demographic?
questions.detail: Ossification of the spinal ligaments, such as OPLL, primarily affects older adults.

questions.question: Ossification of the Posterior Longitudinal Ligament (OPLL) most frequently involves which spinal region?
questions.detail: Ossification of the Posterior Longitudinal Ligament (OPLL) most frequently involves the cervical spinal region.

questions.question: Spondylolysis is defined as a failure or defect of which anatomical structure?
questions.detail: Spondylolysis is defined as a failure or defect of the pars interarticularis.

questions.question: Which imaging modality is considered the most definitive for diagnosing a pars defect?
questions.detail: CT is considered the most definitive imaging modality for diagnosing a pars defect.

questions.question: On an oblique lumbar radiograph, the "neck" of the characteristic "Scotty dog" represents the:
questions.detail: On an oblique lumbar radiograph, the "neck" of the characteristic "Scotty dog" represents the pars interarticularis.

questions.question: Spondylolysis typically results in which type of vertebral slippage?
When spondylolysis causes anterolisthesis, how is the spinal canal traditionally affected?
questions.detail: When spondylolysis causes anterolisthesis, the spinal canal is traditionally widened.

questions.question: If one vertebral pedicle is sclerotic and the other is normal, which of the following is a possible diagnosis?
questions.detail: Possible diagnoses for one sclerotic vertebral pedicle include metastasis, osteoid osteoma, or unilateral spondylolysis with reactive changes.

questions.question: A "unilateral lucent pedicle" on a radiograph, if congenital, is often associated with which finding on the opposite side?
choices: Stress-related sclerosis of the contralateral pedicle
questions.detail: A "unilateral lucent pedicle" on a radiograph, if congenital, is often associated with stress-related sclerosis of the contralateral pedicle.

questions.question: An expansile, lytic mass centered at a pedicle with internal cystic components and fluid-levels is most likely:
questions.detail: An expansile, lytic mass centered at a pedicle with internal cystic components and fluid-levels is most likely an aneurysmal bone cyst (ABC).

questions.question: "Fossa navicularis magna" (noted in Head/Neck but relevant to the skull base/spine junction) is a variant of the:
questions.detail: "Fossa navicularis magna" is a variant of the basiocciput (clivus).
